subject: deal with ordinal endogenous variable with "lavaan"

messages.author: a1805303aff0af2e
messages.subject: deal with ordinal endogenous variable with "lavaan"
parts:
Dear all, I got a question regarding including an ordinal endogenous variable in SEM.

My model looks like this (I have no latent variables):

Model.example<- 'Y1 ~  Y2 + X1 + X2 + X3 + X4
                                 Y2 ~ X1 + X2
                                 Y1 ~~ Y2'

Y2 is an ordinal endogenous variable and it contains 1, 2, 3, 4 to represent four different levels.

According to the instruction, I tried to fit the model like this:

Model.fit <-sem(Model.example, Mydataset, ordered=c("Y2"))

The model did not converge and I received the warning message:

Warning messages:
1: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble inverting W matrix; used generalized inverse
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = Model.example, Mydataset, ordered=c("Y2"),  :
  lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!

My question: is this an issue with my R code? or it is an issue with my model specification?

Any advice is greatly appreciated!

Best

Gary

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: deal with ordinal endogenous variable with "lavaan"
parts:
Gary,
  Your model contains a bow pattern: Y1 ~ Y2 and Y1 ~~ Y2.  However, all the variables that affect Y2 also affect Y1 (i.e., X1 and X2).  That means that none of the other variables provide instrumental variables to identify the parameters involved in the bow pattern.  If you run the model on continuous data, you will encounter the same identification problem.

simModel.example<- 'Y1 ~ .5*Y2 + .5*X1 + .5*X2 + .5*X3 + .5*X4
Y2 ~ .5*X1 + .5*X2
Y1 ~~ .5*Y2'

simData.example <- simulateData(simModel.example)

fitModel.example<- 'Y1 ~ Y2 + X1 + X2 + X3 + X4

Model.fit <-sem(fitModel.example, simData.example)

If you can find a variable that affects Y2 but does not directly affect Y1, then that may allow you to estimate all the parameters.  I am not recommending that you apply the below model to your data (it is presumably misspecified) but just to illustrate:

fitModel.example2<- 'Y1 ~ Y2 + X1 + X2 + X3
Y2 ~ X1 + X2 + X4
Y1 ~~ Y2'

Model.fit2 <-sem(fitModel.example2, simData.example)

This model converges normally.

Keith
